correctness.rationale: On the connected part of the compact feasible weight polytope, the inverse trace of L+J is strictly convex: diagonalizing L+J writes its second variation as a positively weighted sum of squares of the entries of any nonzero perturbation. The cost diverges as support disconnects; uniqueness enforces dihedral invariance among all edge-by-edge feasible walks. An independent check of the reduced objective uses effective resistances. Each pendant edge contributes (2n)/c to the Kirchhoff index; collapse the pendant leaves for the core part, counting each rim vertex twice and the hub once. In the weighted wheel, the sum of core rim-pair resistances is nS, and the sum of hub-rim resistances is 1/a+S, where S=Σ_{k≠0}1/(a+2bt_k): each hub-rim pair has uniform-mode resistance 1/(na) and nonuniform-mode contribution S/n. The core index therefore contributes 4nS+2(1/a+S). Dividing the total index by 2n+1 recovers A_n/c+B_n/a+2S. Increasing b always helps until rim capacity binds. The trial at a=1/n, c=n^(-1/4) and the resolvent comparison with w≤1−ε exclude c≥ε for large n. At fixed c≤1/4 and a≤1/n the sum of (1−t_k)/(a+wt_k)^2 has positive contribution of order n^(5/2) from k≤√n/8, versus negative part O(n). There is a missing factor of two if RESULT.md line 87 is read as the derivative of the entire last term of F_n; its sign is unchanged, and the hub saturation argument uses only the sign. The scalar c-derivative has opposite endpoint signs and is strictly increasing. The exact resolvent can be replayed by expanding (a+w−w cos θ)^(-1) in Fourier coefficients proportional to exp(−|k| acosh(1+a/w)) and averaging at the n grid points. At a=1/n and w→1, differentiating gives −∂_w(2S)∼n^(3/2)/√2, so c_n∼2^(1/4)n^(-1/4). The linear resolvent correction and A_n/c_n each contribute 2^(-1/4)n^(5/4). For the maximum-degree walk the remaining Riemann mean is 1/√5, confirming both comparison constants. This establishes eventual, not explicitly thresholded, hub saturation and the claimed asymptotics only for the stated symmetric stochastic domain and zero-target convention. The bundled finite diagnostics were read, not executed or treated as proof.

value.rationale: A classical graph combines two competing uses of rim probability mass. The optimum has an exact eventual active constraint but an intermediate, non-obvious pendant scale, neither the bare-wheel allocation nor the sunlet scale. The second term identifies the cost of that trade-off, and the diverging maximum-degree benchmark gap gives a concrete reason the optimized allocation matters. This is an asymptotic design result for the specified uniform-stationary family, not a claim about arbitrary routing or a numerical sample.
